chunks: And from him, from Hammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:
"The pilgrim should not take provisions from his sacrificial animal, but he may eat in Mina during its days."
He said: And this is the question of Shihab, which he wrote to him regarding it.

key_terms.أَيَّامَهَا: Its days (referring to the days of Hajj/Tashriq)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules regarding eating from the Hajj sacrificial animal in Mina?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of consuming one's sacrificial animal (udhiyah) in Mina during the days of Tashriq, distinguishing it from the general rule of taking provisions for the journey. It highlights the scholarly consensus on the practical application of Hajj rituals, emphasizing the pilgrim's right to benefit from the sacrifice during the specific holy days. The text also notes the transmission chain's connection to the question of Shihab, reflecting the dynamic nature of fiqh derivation in Shia tradition.
